definitions.explanation: An individual section or stipulation within a contract, law, treaty, or other formal document. Used in legal and business contexts.

examples.japanese: {契約|けいやく}の{条項|じょうこう}を{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: I check the terms of the contract.

examples.japanese: この{条項|じょうこう}に{違反|いはん}した{場合|ばあい}、{罰金|ばっきん}が{科|か}される。
examples.english: If this clause is violated, a fine will be imposed.

examples.japanese: {両国|りょうこく}は{条約|じょうやく}の{一部|いちぶ}の{条項|じょうこう}について{合意|ごうい}に{達|たっ}した。
examples.english: The two countries reached agreement on some provisions of the treaty.

notes: Used in legal, business, and diplomatic contexts. Common collocations: {条項|じょうこう}を{設|もう}ける (establish a provision), {条項|じょうこう}に{基|もと}づく (based on a provision), {免責条項|めんせきじょうこう} (disclaimer clause), {秘密保持条項|ひみつほじじょうこう} (confidentiality clause). Distinguished from {条件|じょうけん} (condition/requirement), which is broader and used in everyday contexts, while {条項|じょうこう} specifically refers to written provisions in formal documents.
